question.problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ with vertices $(-3,-1),(-1,-1),(-1,1),$ and $(-3,1),$ traversed counterclockwise. Using the flux form of Green's theorem, express the flux of the vector field
$F(x,y)=(y{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}x)\,i+(-{y}^{2}x+{y}^{4})\,j$
through $C$ as a repeated integral.
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14224656/assets/5497f23e51d1e745fef1cf39d6c1a8ada22b25e8c9c7b87f5d5338e85a941739.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=y{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}x$ and $Q(x,y)=-{y}^{2}x+{y}^{4}.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2yx+{y}^{3},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2yx+4{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-3\le x\le -1,\,-1\le y\le 1\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2yx+{y}^{3})+(-2yx+4{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}5{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
